title: Edinger-Westphal Neurons Contribute to Emergence from Desflurane and Sevoflurane Anesthesia in Mice.
authors: Hu 胡译文, Yiwen; Huang 黄静, Jing; Bai 白福海, Fuhai; Yang 杨静, Jing; Long 龙宗泓, Zonghong; Li 李钰, Yu; Zhang 张敏, Min; Huang 黄露, Lu; Wu 吴卓熙, Zhuoxi; Yi 易婷婷, Tingting; Li 李洪, Hong
journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
one_liner_zh: 该文研究麻醉剂对Edinger-Westphal神经元激活及GHSR受体在麻醉苏醒中的作用，核心为神经药理学与麻醉机制，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: Most general anesthetics have long been believed to work by exerting a wide range of inhibitory impacts on the central nervous system, yet accumulating evidence has highlighted their excitatory effects-particularly that multiple anesthetics activate a common neural target to induce anesthesia. However, it remains unclear whether three widely used volatile anesthetics (isoflurane, sevoflurane, desflurane) with similar pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic properties share a common brain region for their anesthetic effects, and most receptors mediating the excitatory effects of general anesthetics remain unidentified. To explore the shared excitatory neural targets of common volatile anesthetics, we combined c-Fos staining, targeted recombination in active populations (TRAP), fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) in adult male and female mice, and molecular docking prediction to characterize anesthetic-activated neurons, their cell types, and potential mediating receptors. We found that desflurane and sevoflurane, except isoflurane, significantly increased c-Fos expression in Edinger-Westphal (EW) neurons with high urocortin 1 (UCN1) expression. Chemogenetic inhibition of sevoflurane-activated EW neurons shortened the emergence time from desflurane anesthesia without significantly changing the induction time. Furthermore, growth hormone secretagogue receptor (GHSR) was substantially enriched in both sevoflurane- and desflurane-activated EW neurons, and local knockdown of GHSR in EW neurons accelerated recovery from both anesthetics. These findings suggest that UCN1(+) EW neurons and GHSR contribute greatly to recovery from desflurane and sevoflurane anesthesia.
abstract_zh: 大多数全身麻醉药长期以来被认为通过中枢神经系统产生广泛的抑制性影响来发挥作用，然而越来越多的证据强调了其兴奋性效应——特别是多种麻醉药激活一个共同的神经靶点以诱导麻醉。然而，目前尚不清楚三种广泛使用的挥发性麻醉药（异氟烷、七氟烷、地氟烷）是否具有相似的药代动力学和药效学特性，并共享一个共同的脑区来产生麻醉效应，且介导全身麻醉药兴奋性效应的大多数受体仍未明确。为探索常见挥发性麻醉药的共同兴奋性神经靶点，我们结合c-Fos染色、靶向重组在活性群体（TRAP）、荧光原位杂交（FISH）在成年雄性和雌性小鼠中，以及分子对接预测，来表征麻醉药激活的神经元、其细胞类型及潜在介导受体。我们发现，除异氟烷外，地氟烷和七氟烷显著增加了Edinger-Westphal（EW）神经元中c-Fos的表达，这些神经元具有高表达尿皮质素1（UCN1）。对七氟烷激活的EW神经元进行化学遗传学抑制，缩短了地氟烷麻醉的苏醒时间，而未显著改变诱导时间。此外，生长激素促分泌素受体（GHSR）在七氟烷和地氟烷激活的EW神经元中均显著富集，且EW神经元中GHSR的局部敲低加速了两种麻醉药的恢复。这些发现表明，UCN1(+) EW神经元和GHSR对地氟烷和七氟烷麻醉的恢复有重要贡献。
